title: Integral lattice pairs, embedded images, class presentations and matrix cosets
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with its small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $R,S$ be sheaves of commutative rings on this site, $a:R\to S$ a ring-sheaf morphism, and $L$ a sheaf of $S$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For $U$ in the site, write $a_U:R|_U\to S|_U$ for restriction to the slice site. An integral lattice pair over $U$ consists of a finite locally free $R|_U$-module $M$ (locally free with finite, possibly varying rank, including zero) and an isomorphism $\alpha:S|_U\otimes_{R|_U}M\xrightarrow{\sim}L|_U$, where scalar extension is the sheafified tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Two pairs $P,Q$ are equivalent when there exists an $R|_U$-module isomorphism $e:M_P\xrightarrow{\sim}M_Q$ with $\alpha_Q\circ(S|_U\otimes e)=\alpha_P$. For a test object $T$ of the slice, define the image of $P$ to be the range in $(L|_U)(T)$ of $m\mapsto\alpha_P(\eta_T(1\otimes m))$, where $\eta$ is the module sheafification unit [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Given a sheaf of sets $F$ and maps $c_U$ from pairs over $U$ to $F(U)$, say that $(F,c)$ is a lattice-class presentation if (i) every $c_U$ is surjective, (ii) $c_U(P)=c_U(Q)$ if and only if $P,Q$ are equivalent, and (iii) for every site morphism $f:V\to U$ and pairs $P$ over $U$, $Q$ over $V$, the equality $F(f)c_U(P)=c_V(Q)$ holds if and only if, on every test object $T$ of the slice over $V$, the image of $P$ on the composed object $T\to V\to U$ equals the image of $Q$ on $T$. For a field $K$, a subring $A\subseteq K$ and $n\in\mathbf N$, define the integral matrix subgroup $H$ to be the image of $\mathrm{GL}_n(A)\to\mathrm{GL}_n(K)$ induced by the inclusion, and define the integral matrix coset set to be $\mathrm{GL}_n(K)/H$, consisting of cosets $gH$ (orbits of right multiplication). With $X:\mathrm{Scheme}_u$, the ring and module section carriers lie in $\mathrm{Type}_{u+1}$ and $F$ takes values in $\mathrm{Type}_{u+2}$.
